subject: Orchard Health — reconciliation and amortization options for Q3 overage
messages:
From: Susan Lane <susan.lane@orchardhealth.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-15T09:02:00-08:00
Subject: Unexpected one-time charge on Nov invoice

Hi Karthik,

We noticed a one-time line item on our November invoice for $18,420 labelled 'retro usage Q3' — this was a surprise to our procurement team. Can you send a breakdown (dates, model hours, region) and let us know if Redwood will consider spreading this over time? We signed a reserved capacity package earlier this year and expected smoother smoothing on spikes.

We need this by COB Monday to get internal approval.

Thanks,
Susan Lane
Director, Cloud Operations
Orchard Health

Attachment: (requested) detailed usage report — we didn't get one in the invoice bundle
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Susan Lane <susan.lane@orchardhealth.com>
Cc: procure@orchardhealth.com
Date: 2026-11-15T10:27:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Unexpected one-time charge on Nov invoice

Hi Susan — thanks for flagging this and sorry for the surprise. I've pulled the initial reconciliation and attached a CSV with per-day model-hours and peak windows (usage_report_q3.csv). Short summary: there was a two-week sustained burst in Sept associated with a batch inference job that bypassed your reserved instances due to an orchestration mis-tag; the net overage mapped to the $18,420 figure.

Options we can do immediately: 
- One-time invoice (current state) — due Net30.
- Amortize the charge over 6 months (we issue 6 smaller invoices).
- Apply a partial credit (10%) if Orchard commits to an additional 6-month capacity top-up starting Jan 1.

I'll loop in our CS and finance owners to finalize which path minimizes friction for you. Are you open to amortization?

Regards,
Karthik Iyer
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Attachments: usage_report_q3.csv
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-16T08:10:00-08:00
Subject: Internal: Orchard Health true-up — options and ask

Folks — Orchard flagged a $18.4k retro charge for Sept. They want alternatives to the one-time. Quick ask: recommend commercial posture. Notes: 
- Account is mid-market, growing inference usage ~18% q/q.
- They have a 12-month reserved capacity expiring 2027-06-30.
- Procurement wants predictable cashflow.

My preference: offer amortize over 6 months by default (reduces friction), and sweeten with a 10% one-time credit only if they commit to an additional reserved increment (6 GPUs equivalent) for 12 months starting Jan. Finance: will amortization require any special contract amendment? Monica: can you draft the amendment and confirm the credit math? Vivek: opinion on precedent for this sort of amortization (exec approval if >$15k credit).

Thanks,
Karthik
From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-16T11:45:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Internal: Orchard Health true-up — options and ask

Karthik — agreed on amortization as primary. Quick answers: 
- Finance: amortization is fine; we'll split into 6 invoices (no change to ARR). I attached a one-page amendment template that adds a payment schedule which we'd send to the customer (draft_amendment_orchard.docx).
- Credit: 10% off the $18,420 = $1,842. We'd only apply if they sign to add 6 GPU-equivalent reserved capacity for 12 months. This is a reasonable trade for expansion.
- Precedent: we've done similar amortizations for three customers this year; execs only needed to sign off when the credit > $25k. So no exec sign-off required here.

I'll prepare the amendment and a clean invoice schedule for their procurement. Recommend we present two commercial paths to Orchard (A = amortize, B = amortize + 10% credit with commit).

-Monica
Senior Revenue Ops Manager, Redwood Inference
Attachment: draft_amendment_orchard.docx
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Susan Lane <susan.lane@orchardhealth.com>
Cc: procure@orchardhealth.com, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-17T14:05:00-08:00
Subject: Orchard Health — proposed resolution for Q3 retro usage (options)

Hi Susan — thanks again for the quick turnaround. Per our reconciliation (attached), the $18,420 true-up comes from 2026-09-12 through 2026-09-26 where an orchestration job missed reservation tagging. We apologize for the operational friction.

We can move forward with either of the following, please let me know which you prefer: 

Option 1 — Standard one-time invoice
- Amount: $18,420 (invoice released today)
- Terms: Net30
- No change to your contract.

Option 2 — Amortized schedule (recommended)
- Amount: $18,420 split across 6 monthly invoices = $3,070 each (Nov 2026 — Apr 2027)
- No interest; invoices will reference amendment #1 (attached) for schedule.

Option 3 — Amortize + expansion credit (preferred for pricing)
- Same amortization as Option 2.
- One-time credit of 10% ($1,842) applied across the first two amortized invoices ($921 credit each).
- Condition: Orchard signs amendment to add 6 GPU-equivalent reserved capacity beginning 2027-01-01 for 12 months (term amendment).

Next steps:
- If you pick Option 2 we will send the amendment form and schedule for signature; the first amortized invoice posts on Nov 20.
- If you pick Option 3 we will attach the expanded capacity SOW for countersignature and apply the credit once we have countersigned paperwork.

Attachments: usage_report_q3.csv, draft_amendment_orchard.docx

Happy to hop on a 15-minute call if your procurement team needs to review.

Best,
Karthik Iyer
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Office: +1 415-555-0164
From: Susan Lane <susan.lane@orchardhealth.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: procure@orchardhealth.com
Date: 2026-11-18T09:20:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Orchard Health — proposed resolution for Q3 retro usage (options)

Karthik — thanks for the clear options and the CSV. Orchard will take Option 2 (amortize over 6 months). Please send the amendment and the schedule to our procurement inbox (procure@orchardhealth.com); they need the invoice schedule for their cashflow planning. We are not ready to commit to additional reserved capacity at this time.

Appreciate the fast response.

—Susan
